summary: The note is an investigative report on how the city of Millennialville has tried to involve young people in local decision-making since a council resolution on September 13, 2023. It describes initiatives including a school curriculum, Young Citizens' Assemblies, mentorship and internships, and the 'SpeakUp!' online platform. It reviews participation and representation figures, policy outcomes such as the climate policy and student fares, and challenges and criticisms.
one_line: Report on Millennialville's initiatives since 2023 to involve youth in local governance, their results, representation gaps, and challenges.
key_facts: Millennialville's city council enacted a landmark resolution on September 13, 2023 to involve youth in decision-making.
The United Nations says there are 1.8 billion young people (aged 10-24) in the world, the largest youth population ever.
Jane Smith, a professor of political science at Millennialville University, says youth involvement is not about tokenism or meeting quotas.
City Councilor John Doe spearheaded the resolution and said it is about building a framework that lowers barriers of entry for young people.

The Collaborative Curriculum, introduced November 15, 2023, is a partnership between local schools and the council for high school seniors, including shadowing council members and mock council meetings.
The first Young Citizens' Assembly was piloted on January 6, 2024 for people aged 16-25, with a month-long deliberation before presenting recommendations to the council.
The city council must respond to each Young Citizens' Assembly suggestion, explaining how it will be considered or why it will not.
Mentorship and internship programs launched on February 20, 2024, pairing youth with local government officials.
The online platform 'SpeakUp!' launched on April 1, 2024 for feedback, discussions with policymakers, and youth proposals.
The Collaborative Curriculum enrolled over 300 students in its first year, and Young Citizens' Assemblies had about 70% attendance.
Only 22% of participants in the latest Young Citizens' Assembly came from disadvantaged socioeconomic backgrounds.
A new climate change policy passed July 21, 2024 was heavily influenced by the first Young Citizens' Assembly, including more green spaces and better public transportation.
Reduced public transport fares for students and young adults, based on 'SpeakUp!' suggestions, took effect October 10, 2024.
Critics argue the initiatives risk creating a parallel structure lacking the power to effect real change, while proponents call them vital stepping stones.
